notes: 1) Test weakness: test_direction_counts_each_disagreement_once uses symmetric data (2 and 2), so swapping the two labels in agreement.direction passes all 12 tests. The code is correct (my recompute gives local_kinder 141 and 28 served), but the headline claim that the local judge is kinder is not protected by a test, and check_run recomputes with the same function so it would not catch an inversion either. Worth an asymmetric case. 2) The Sonnet prompt text is passed through clean(), which removes control characters, so it can differ slightly from what the local judge saw; no row was affected as far as I checked, but it is unmeasured. 3) Blind-file passages are cut mid-sentence at about 1,000 characters and both graders see the cut text; disease names can fall outside the chunk (supported-031 [5]). 4) DECISIONS says Sonnet graded six of seven supported on supported-031 so a per-claim check doesn't catch the transfer; Sonnet's one no sat on half of the transfer (claim 3), though for the wrong-citation reason. 5) The adjudication is one reader, with most calls close. The result favours neither grader on served splits and favours Sonnet on non-served ones, with a wide interval (n=20). 6) Process: I accidentally started two idle interactive python REPLs from a stray heredoc; they were never given input and I could not stop them with the available tools; they hold no state. Not stopped by name or image. 7) No Claude calls, no GPU, no Ollama used by me; test runs went one at a time through one_test.py.
